name: Abdul Alhazred, the Mad Sorcerer
description:
Abdul Alhazred is renowned as the mad sorcerer from the Arabian town of Sanaa. Born to wealthy merchants he was educated with the sons of the local Caliph and it was in the Caliph's private library that be first learnt about the land of the Dead from tomes he had been expressly forbidden to read. It was then that he developed an obsessional desire for knowledge of the long dead civilisation of Nehekhara and some say it was the dread reputation of this ancient land that drew him on to rash acts. Others say it was the calling of the legendary Nagash none know...

It is said that he left immediately, stealing enough money to fund his wanderings along with an artefact of such antiquity it was believed to have come from Nehekhara. He has visited the ruins of Khemri, Zandri, Numas and Quatar and over long years plundered them of their secrets. His discoveries rival those of Abdul Ben Raschid, whose works he has voraciously studied and it is these that have sent him spiralling into insanity. Referred to as 'The Mad Sorcerer' he is shunned by all except those foolish enough to want to learn the secrets of the Land of the Dead.

specials.name: The Eye Pendant
specials.description: The Eye Pendant is an ancient artefact stolen by Abdul from the Caliph of Sanai. Only after much painstaking research did Abdul discover its secrets and he has used its arcane powers to protect himself from the wrath of the Tomb Kings and their servants. Any Undead warrior wishing to attack Abdul must first pass a Ld test. In addition, the pendant gives Abdul a 4+ Ward save against all damage.

specials.name: Psychology
specials.description: Abdul Alhazred has witnessed some of the foulest monstrosities of the Land of the Dead and is quite mad! He is immune to all Psychology-tests.

specials.name: Djinn Master
specials.description: Abdul Afhazred has spoken to many of the mystical Djinn in his time and despite his unsteady state of mind knows how to see through their lies and bend them to his will. If the warband he is with acquires a Lamp of the Djinn he may assist a Hero using it with a +1/-1 modifier on the Light and Dark tables respectively.

specials.name: Master Wizard
specials.description:
The Mad Arab is one of the most learned and powerful wizards in Araby. He knows all the spells in the Elemental lists. Because he is mad, however, he must roll at the beginning of each Shooting phase to see which spell he remembers.

Roll a D6: 1-3 Elemental, 4-6 Necromancy

Then roll a D6 to see which spell be remembers.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: All warbands, except Witch Hunters and Sisters of Sigmar, may hire the Mad Sorcerer.

name: Aenur, the Sword of Twilight
description:
Many famous swordsmen have come to Mordheim to make their fortune, but few can match the terrifying reputation of the Elf swordsman Aenur. This mighty warrior was responsible for slaying the entire Possessed warband of Karl Zimmeran, and single-handedly cleansed the Rat Hole, a settlement that had been overrun by Beastmen.

Rumours about Aenur’s origin abound. Elves usually avoid human settlements, and Mordheim in particular, but for some reason the tall, pale swordsman has stayed in the proximity of the ruined city for months.

Some say Aenur comes from beyond the Great Ocean, from the fabled Elven kingdoms, and that he is the captain of the legendary Order of Swordmasters. Others claim that he is a Wood Elf prince in exile. Aenur himself says little about his past and those who are wise do not question him.

Whenever a warband prepares an expedition to explore the inner city, there is a chance they may hear a sharp rap at the gate of their encampment – their unexpected visitor will be Aenur, offering his services to their leader.

If, indeed, Aenur seeks something in the grim ruins of Mordheim, no-one knows what this might be. Some say that he wishes to explore the Pit itself, and slay the enigmatic Shadow Lord, though such a task must surely be above even this mighty warrior.

Aenur is tall even for an Elf, and beneath his finely woven Elven cloak he wears armour of gleaming ithilmar. He carries a sword of immense size which is rumoured to have arcane properties. Certainly no one who has been struck by it has ever lived to tell the tale.

specials.name: Invincible Swordsman
specials.description: Aenur always hits his opponents on a roll of 2+ in hand-to-hand combat.

specials.name: Wanderer
specials.description: Aenur only ever stays with a warband for the duration of the battle. A warband who used Aenur in their last battle may not seek him out until they have fought at least one battle without him.

specials.name: Ienh-Khain (the Hand of Khaine)
specials.description: Ienh-Khain is an incredibly long single-edged sword, which Aenur uses with consummate skill. This sword allows Aenur to parry, adds +1 to his Strength and causes a critical hit on a roll of 5-6 when rolling to wound.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven, Undead and the Possessed may hire Aenur.

name: Aksho'akhash the Vile Dreadwing, Lord of the Carrion Throne
description:
Upon completing an intricate summoning ritual involving one dead goat, two pinches of wyrdstone powder, and a grisly book of Chaos Magic most foul, the air takes an odour of sulfur and from an explosion of fresh goat blood a horrifying visage appears, though not the one that was expected.

The obscure tales of this “Daemon Lord” seem to have been greatly exaggerated; Aksho'akhash the “Vile Dreadwing” and “Lord of the Carrion Throne” appears to be nothing but a typical Chaos Fury that is somewhat more cunning than others of its kind and has a kleptomaniacal obsession for hoarding bits of garbage that only an insane Daemon could see the value of.

It is quickly apparent that any “immense treasure hoard of legend” that this Lesser Daemon might possess would not contain anything useful to a mortal, but perhaps one could put this interdimensional scavenger’s skills to good use in exploring the ruins of the City of the Damned.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: Lesser Daemons are horrifying supernatural creatures that cause fear in all who gaze upon them.

specials.name: Daemonic Flesh
specials.description: Due to their intangible nature, Daemons have a base armour save of 5+. This save is never modified but is completely negated by blessed or magic weapons and spells. The Daemon's attacks also count as magical.

specials.name: Daemonic Instability
specials.description: Daemons are bound to the world by dark sorcery that is highly volatile and unstable. If taken out of action, Aksho'akhash is banished and effectively destroyed on a D6 roll of 1-3 (do not roll for injury). If the spell-caster that summoned the Daemon is killed or leaves the warband, the Daemon is banished from whence it came.

specials.name: Coward King
specials.description: One does not grow to become ruler of a rubbish heap without a healthy respect for the integrity of one’s corporeal form. Unlike other Daemons of its ilk, Aksho'akhash is not immune to any psychology. Additionally, unlike other warriors that cause fear, Aksho'akhash itself is not immune to fear tests caused by other warriors.

specials.name: Fly
specials.description:
Instead of moving normally (unless knocked down or stunned), Aksho'akhash may choose to:
- Move anywhere within 12" including into base contact with an enemy (in which case it counts as charging).
- Move vertically without needing to climb.
- Jump from any height without falling.

specials.name: Aethereal Hoarder
specials.description:
Aksho'akhash has spent millennia picking through debris across the cosmos. While no mortal mind could comprehend exactly why such objects compel his attention, his skills for finding a diamond in the rough are valuable indeed.

After each game, so long as Aksho'akhash was not taken out of action, it may perform one of the following tasks:
- Reroll one exploration dice.
- Search for a rare item as if it was a Hero; add 1 to the roll.
- Find trinkets amongst the ruins worth 2D6 gold crowns.

hire_fee.note: All warbands devoted to Chaos (such as the Cult of Possessed and Beastmen Raiders) may attempt to hire Aksho'akhash by having a spell-caster in the warband attempt a summoning ritual once after each game. The spell-caster must possess the Macabre Tome from the ‘Flurry of Furies’ scenario (see the previous page), pay the hiring fee*, and pass a Leadership test. If the ritual is successful, the Macabre Tome is destroyed and the Daemon is summoned.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: All warbands devoted to Chaos (such as the Cult of Possessed and Beastmen Raiders) may attempt to hire Aksho'akhash by having a spell-caster in the warband attempt a summoning ritual once after each game. The spell-caster must possess the Macabre Tome from the ‘Flurry of Furies’ scenario (see the previous page), pay the hiring fee*, and pass a Leadership test. If the ritual is successful, the Macabre Tome is destroyed and the Daemon is summoned.

specials.name: Sought Out
specials.description:
There is no hire fee. He comes to the aid of a warband that may hire him only if it sends one or more of its heroes to look for him in the normal manner, rolling under or equal to their Initiative. Found, he may still decide not to come, and comes only if the enemy warband has the higher rating. Roll a D6 and consult the table.

Difference in warband rating | D6 needed
0-49 | no chance
50-99 | 6+
100-149 | 5+
150-199 | 4+
200+ | 3+

specials.name: Facing Skaven
specials.description: Add 1 to the roll if the warband faces Skaven. If the opposing warband has hired Neekit, Alchec comes on a 5+ whatever the difference in ratings.

specials.name: Vampire
specials.description: Alchec is subject to all the normal vampire rules.

specials.name: Bestial
specials.description: Alchec has a 6+ ward save against all attacks.

specials.name: No Magic
specials.description: Although a Strigoi vampire, Alchec's animal nature stops him using magic.

specials.name: Strigoi Lord
specials.description: Alchec is automatically the leader of any warband he joins.

specials.name: Infinite Hatred
specials.description: Alchec may re-roll all failed to-hit rolls in the first round of each combat. Each dice may be re-rolled only once.

specials.name: Blood Lust
specials.description: Alchec is subject to frenzy.

hire_fee.note: No hire fee: he must be sought out before the battle.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any Strigoi or Strigany warband may hire Alchec.

name: Belandysh, Condemned Champion of Chen
description:
Belandysh was once a powerful Chaos Champion and Chieftain to the Tribe of the Rising Eagle, notable for their devotion to Chen, as Tchar is known amongst the Hung. When he turned from Chen’s paths, the Lord of Change blessed Belandysh in punishment, mutating the champion into a living symbol of constant change, gifting Belandysh a powerful blade that would deform his enemies into Chaos Spawn. Now he perfectly represents his former patron and can never be free, save in death. Perhaps that is the way the Master of Transfiguration meant for Belandysh to be after all.

Also carries: Broadsword of Damnation.
Also has: Ride.

specials.name: Immune to psychology
specials.description: Belandysh is immune to psychology and automatically passes all Leadership tests.

specials.name: Inconsistency
specials.description: Belandysh's body is mutating permanently. His variable attributes are determined whenever needed, once every turn.

specials.name: Regeneration
specials.description: Whenever an enemy successfully inflicts a wound on Belandysh, roll a D6, on a result of 4 or more the wound is ignored and Belandysh unhurt. However, note that he may not regenerate wounds caused by fire or fire-based magic.

specials.name: Tol'Agath
specials.description: Belandysh used to ride a normal Battle Horse when he was still a Marauder Chieftain. When turned into a Chaos spawn, Tol'Agath, his steed, was hardly spared and mutated as well. Tol'Agath acts as a Warhorse (including the Battle Schooled rule). In addition, it is subject to the Inconsistency special rule.

specials.name: Wrath of Tchar
specials.description: If a battle ends with Belandysh being out of action and someone having picked up the Broadsword of Damnation, Belandysh is pulled into the Realm of Chaos and never seen again. He then cannot be hired again for the remainder of the campaign.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Marauders of Chaos, Beastmen, Norse and Possessed may hire Belandysh.

name: Bertha Bestraufrung, High Matriarch of the Sisterhood
description:
Years ago, Bertha sought refuge in the strict discipline and devotions of the Sisters of Sigmar. Only the warrior god of the Empire was worthy of her esteem. Only He was constant and faithful. And had not holy Sigmar, in truth, chosen her to be one of his handmaidens?

The pure blood of the Unberogens runs in Bertha’s veins, as evinced by her long golden plaits and fierce blue eyes, which can freeze a Goblin at twenty paces with an icy glare. Even her voice commands authority, turning strong, hairy-thewed men into trembling wretches.

The Sisters look up to Bertha as an example of holy womanhood. She rose rapidly through the ranks of the Sisterhood, and on her deathbed the revered Matriarch Cassandra named Bertha her successor, new High Matriarch, and Abedissa of Sigmar’s Rock.

Sometimes, as Bertha straps on her Gromril armour in the light of dawn, she reflects on the lost innocence of her youth. Then, angrily, she tightens the studded leather straps tightly over her iron-hard limbs and strides outside to spend hours practising with her great warhammers, preparing herself, as a bride of Sigmar should, for the day of battle.

Extract from the Tome of Heroes

Also carries: Holy Relic.

specials.name: Hiring Fee
specials.description:
None. Bertha will come to the aid of any Sisters of Sigmar warband if they send one or more of their Heroines to look for her in the normal manner, rolling under their Initiative (representing their efforts to gain audience with the High Matriarch). If she does grant an audience, she might decide that her personal help is needed in the forthcoming battle. She will only come to the aid of a Sisters of Sigmar warband if their enemy has a higher warband rating. Consult the table below, and roll a D6 to see whether Bertha will aid the warband. A request for Bertha to aid the warband must be made for each battle you wish her to help the warband.

Difference in Warband Rating: Dice roll required
0-49: Nil
50-99: 6+
100-149: 5+
150-199: 4+
200+: 3+

specials.name: High Matriarch
specials.description: As the High Matriarch of the Sisters of Sigmar’s Mercy, Bertha will automatically be the leader of any warband she joins.

specials.name: Sigmar’s Handmaiden
specials.description: Bertha is favoured above all other Sisters in the eyes of Sigmar. She gains +2 to all her rolls to see whether her Prayers of Sigmar are granted.

specials.name: Spells
specials.description: Bertha knows all six Prayers of Sigmar.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Bertha Bestraufrung will only join Sisters of Sigmar warbands.

name: Billie Rattenmörder and Butcher
description: Billie, the last of Mordheim's ratcatchers, and her dog Butcher. The row's profile is Billie's.

specials.name: Hated Ratmen
specials.description: Billie hates Skaven. When fighting against Skaven she is also subject to frenzy, and she must always pick members of a Skaven warband over other enemies to charge.

specials.name: Small But Vicious Dog
specials.description: Butcher's profile is M6 WS4 BS0 S4 T3 W1 I4 A1 Ld5. His bite causes a critical hit on a roll of 5-6 when rolling to wound.

specials.name: Fiercely Loyal
specials.description: If Billie is taken out of action, place a marker where she falls. Butcher must move as quickly as he can to that spot, and once he gets there he must stay within a number of inches of it equal to his Leadership for the rest of the game, guarding her body. All his attacks are subject to hatred until the end of the battle.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Only Human Mercenaries and Witch Hunters can hire Billie and Butcher.

name: Countess Marianna Chevaux, Vampire Assassin
description:
Once an assassin-thief, Marianna’s ambitions outreached her. In a daring expedition to Araby, she came into contact with the ancient Vampiress Serutat. Marianna succeeded in her mission, stealing the gem, the Noctu, from Serutat’s crypt but the Vampiress caught up with her, tainting her with the curse of Vampirism before the resourceful assassin could escape.

In a moment Marianna had become a thing of the night and yet she was not completely damned, a half-vampire. Sating her bloodlust on the numerous courtesans, captains and suitors that came her way, Marianna fled the bitter vengeance of the Lahmian Vampire, Serutat, to Mordheim. With the City of the Damned her relative anonymity would be assured.

Marianna is a pragmatist, neutral in her persona, serving only her own means, hiring her skills out as an assassin, taking care to conceal her secret. Wary of witch hunters and the other devout servants of Sigmar, Marianna is a creature of the shadows, her vampiric powers enhancing her abilities immeasurably. And yet the flight to Mordheim serves an ulterior motive. Vampire turned Vampire Hunter and as such an exile in the dark Undead underworld, Marianna tracks the night-stalkers of Mordheim, torturing them for information; the whereabouts of Serutat and the true nature of the Noctu, the black jewel stolen from her crypt. Marianna’s efforts have borne dark fruit, a word of power and the stone will create a veil of shadow to cloak the bearer, drifting like a black ether. Marianna means to seek out Serutat in her lair when she is vulnerable, exacting her own vengeance for damning her to darkness, her ‘interrogations’ warning her that the Vampire has travelled to the Empire to settle the score and retrieve the Noctu. A plethora of aliases have kept Marianna hidden so far but occasionally, during a battle in the deepest recesses of the city, minions of Serutat will appear out of the night to exact their mistress’s vengeance, much to the surprise of the vying warbands. Marianna walks a dagger-thin line but thus far she has yet to slip…

Also carries: Throwing Knives.

specials.name: Immune to Psychology
specials.description: As a Vampire, Marianna is completely immune to the effects of psychology and will never leave combat.

specials.name: Immune to Poison
specials.description: As a Vampire, Marianna is completely immune to the effects of poison.

specials.name: No Pain
specials.description: Marianna treats a stunned result on the Injury chart as knocked down instead (note that with her Jump Up ability Marianna cannot be knocked down either so the only way to stop her is to take her out of action!).

specials.name: Cause fear
specials.description: Marianna is a terrifying creature, although more through reputation than her being a Vampire as she is contriving to keep her identity a secret.

specials.name: ‘You can never escape your past…’
specials.description:
On the last turn of the game in which Marianna is still standing or as soon as a warband routs, ending the game, roll a D6:

D6: Result
1-3: Marianna has discovered that Serutat is getting close and will leave the warband’s service after the game.
4-5: Marianna has discovered a useful lead that she must pursue in this area and will stay for another game if the warband can afford her upkeep.
6: A group of Serutat’s minions have caught up with her! Fight D3 more turns as if the losing warband hadn’t routed (in the confusion the balance is reset). A randomly determined group of minions ‘appear’ within 2D6" of Marianna, the opposing player chooses where. Marianna takes the first turn and then the minions, after which the turn sequence returns to normal with the minions counted as a an extra player. The minions only attack Marianna and must move towards her as fast as possible but will attack anyone else in their way. If her warband fight to help her (by taking at least one minion out of action) and she survives, Marianna will fight the next battle for free, otherwise she will leave.

D6: Minions
1-2: D3+1 Zombies
3-4: D3+1 Ghouls
5-6: Vampire (Sword & light armour) +2 Ghouls

specials.name: Fighting Undead
specials.description: Due to her vocation as a Vampire Assassin turned Vampire Hunter, all Vampires hate Marianna.

specials.name: The Noctu
specials.description: The gemstone stolen from Serutat’s lair has powerful cloaking properties. The veil of shadow it creates reduces all shooting to hit rolls against Marianna by -1.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any Warband except Witch Hunters, Sisters of Sigmar, Undead, Elves and other Sigmar devoted warbands may hire Marianna (note, mercenaries are men of lax faith and do not count here).

specials.name: Hates Skaven
specials.description: The model hates all Skaven.

specials.name: No Slayer Oath
specials.description: Dalla follows the Dwarf rules of the Mordheim rulebook and the Karak Azgal setting, except the Karak Azgal rule for becoming a Slayer. The Slayer Cult is a male tradition, so where that rule would apply she gains hatred of that warband from then on instead, since she cannot redeem herself by becoming a Slayer.

specials.name: Come On Boys!
specials.description: If Dalla charges an enemy model or group, any male Dwarf model may charge the same model, or one within 2" of it, and makes its attacks at +1 Strength in the first round.

specials.name: Look At Her Fight!
specials.description: Any Dwarf model within 6" of Dalla attacks first in the second round only of any close combat it is in.

specials.name: Goblin's Bane
specials.description: A large gromril Dwarf axe that Dalla uses as a double-handed weapon, gaining the normal +1 Strength but attacking in normal order instead of last. It also has the advantages of a Dwarf axe (parry) and of a gromril weapon. If captured it counts as a normal gromril Dwarf axe, and all Dwarfs of Karak Azgal hate a warrior using it as a captured weapon. If a warband authorised by Kargan to explore Karak Azgal recaptures it, it may be sold back to Kargan for twice the normal selling price.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any Dwarf or human warband may hire Dalla.

name: Dark Emissary
description:
Of all the mysteries of Albion perhaps the greatest is the purpose of the enigmatic figures known as Dark Emissaries and Truthsayers. These ancient wizards are erstwhile enemies and their secret battle hints at a greater struggle yet to pass. Dark Emissaries, servants of the Dark Master, a powerful and enigmatic figure are potentates of evil. They ally themselves with evil forces and seek to harness the power of the Ogham Stones for all manner of unknown and nefarious practices. Truthsayers, the druidic warrior-wizards, the benevolent protectors of the Ogham magic grant their aid and wisdom to the followers of Sigmar and his allies, their only purpose to thwart the Dark Master and his lackeys.

Dark Emissaries and Truthsayers feature in the scenario The Ogham Stones but if players wish they may be sought out for each battle in Albion in the same manner as Dramatis Persona. There is no hire fee for either character as they have their own agenda for joining the battle.

However, wherever there is one the other will surely follow. If a warband successfully finds either a Dark Emissary or Truthsayer and the other warband does not then roil a D6 at the start of that warband's turn, on a roil of 4+ the opposing character appears to fight alongside the warband and is deployed at a random table edge (see 'Surprise Attack' for details). If the opposing warbands are both of 'evil' or 'good' alignment then the Dark Emissary or Truthsayer may not be sought out for the battle.

specials.name: Staff of Darkness
specials.description: + 1 to his casting roll.

specials.name: The Spiral
specials.description: A symbol of the Dark Master. It is a potent icon that protects the wearer from harm. It grants the Dark Emissary a 5+ save that cannot be reduced by anything.

specials.name: Wizard
specials.description: The Dark Emissary is a powerful spell caster and knows four randomly determined spells of the Lore of Darkness.

specials.name: Alignment
specials.description: Dark Emissaries are evil wizards and as such will only fight alongside Possessed, Undead, Skaven and other evilly aligned warbands.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Dark Emissaries are evil wizards and as such will only fight alongside Possessed, Undead, Skaven and other evilly aligned warbands.

specials.name: Sought Out by the Weak
specials.description:
The Dashing Swordsman seeks no payment, but protects only the weak, and only those who really need his help. He joins a warband only if its rating is lower than its opponent's. Roll a dice and consult the table.

Difference in warband rating | Dice needed
0-49 | auto-failure
50-99 | 6+
100-149 | 5+
150-199 | 4+
200-249 | 3+
250-299 | 2+
300 or more | auto-success

specials.name: You Want My Help, Madam?
specials.description: Add 1 to the roll for him to come for each female model in the warband, counting auto-failure as 7+.

specials.name: Wait, My Hero!
specials.description: After the battle the Dashing Swordsman vanishes. After determining injuries, but before allocating experience, each female model in the warband must pass a Leadership test on her own Leadership. A model that fails leaves the warband at once in pursuit of him and counts as dead. If the warband was defeated even with him in it, no tests are taken at all.

specials.name: I Challenge You!
specials.description: The Dashing Swordsman must move towards the closest enemy warrior as far as he can and charge him if he can. He cannot charge an enemy who cannot see him.

specials.name: Touché!
specials.description: The Dashing Swordsman may name one enemy model in base contact in the combat phase and take a Leadership test. If he passes, that model is confused and he is at +1 to hit and to wound it. If he fails, he is at -1 to hit and to wound it. This may not be used on undead other than vampires, on daemons, on animals or on a model that has failed a Stupidity test.

specials.name: His Sharpened Skills
specials.description: His Expert Swordsman lets him re-roll missed hits when he charges. His Acrobat lets him make a diving charge from 12" and take only one Initiative test to do so, which may be re-rolled. His Dodge and Step Aside saves are both 4+.

specials.name: Cloak
specials.description: His cloak lets him fall further: he may make a diving charge on models within D6" of where he lands.

specials.name: Exquisite Rapier
specials.description: Turn Aside Blow: when an opponent hits the Dashing Swordsman in close combat, roll a dice; if the score is lower than his Weapon Skill, that opponent's first hit has no effect. Barrage: if he hits an enemy but does not wound him, he may make one more attack for each hit that did not wound, and may keep doing so as long as he hits and does not wound. Armour saves against it are at -1. Master-crafted: he cannot be disarmed and the weapon cannot be destroyed.

hire_fee.note: No payment: he must be sought out, and comes only to the weaker warband.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: The Dashing Swordsman will join only good-aligned warbands.

name: Dijin Katal, the Renegade Assassin
description:
How many years have I walked the earth? How many plains have I seen that stretch to the horizon? How many cities are there that are crammed with the filth and dregs of this world? And how many dark places have been my refuges? Yet I still miss that dreaded place Clar Karond... my home. I wonder what is happening amongst my kin what devious politics abound. Oh, how I miss the intrigue of a true civilisation. These are strange times. I never desired to travel to this hot insect-infested land of Lustria but now I am here it has a strange hold on me. I have delivered many to the grace of Khaine within this jungle. This jungle seems to cry out for blood. Although my murderous instincts have grown the animal inside is now in sated. What has become of me?

Still, my blades run with the blood of my enemies the only thing that brings me comfort. I have the murderous instinct, which my people have practised for thousands of years and the addiction is strong. That night when I saw the broken bodies of my own kin on the floor in the carnival of horrors I knew that killing was my sole purpose. I also knew that it didn't matter who would be my prey - friend or foe it makes no difference to the unquenchable thirst within. And now my comrades hunt me. Although my thirst for another murder is great in good time soon it shall be quenched. My life is for Khaine.

My goal? To find some meaning to this mundane existence...

Known as 'The Hunter in the Shadows', 'The Thrice Cursed Renegade', 'He who Thirsts' and 'Kinslayer', among other things, Dijin Katal as greatly feared and loathed and that's just by his own people. The covens of the Druchii have a price on Katal's head and demand that he be captured alive for the Hag Queen's pleasure. Few know this Druchii's chequered past when they hire him in fact most are not even aware that he is Druchii, such is their ignorance.

Also carries: Assassin's Cloak.

specials.name: Kindred Hatred
specials.description: The Dark Elves have been fighting the High Elves for many centuries. The wars between the two races have been very long and bloody affairs. The Dark Elves are very bitter since they have been exiled from Ulthuan and thus they hate any High Elf warriors including High Elf Hired Swords.

specials.name: Excellent Sight
specials.description: There are numerous legends detailing the excellent eyesight of the Elves, both Druchii and Ulthuan kin. Elves can spot hidden enemies from twice as far away than normal warriors (i.e. twice their Initiative value in inches).

specials.name: Shadows Embrace
specials.description: The Dark Elf has mastered the art of making the best use of shadows to hide, this is the legendary ability of the Dark Elf Scouts and the Assassins. If the Dark Elf is in cover and a model attempts to charge him, he can only charge the Elf using a charge move equal to his initiative in inches. In addition, missile weapons suffer an additional -1 penalty to hit on top of the penalty for cover.

specials.name: Perfect Killer
specials.description: All attacks made by the Assassin, whether in shooting or close combat, have an extra -1 save modifier to represent his skill In striking at unarmoured spots.

specials.name: Renegade
specials.description: Dijin is a kinslayer and therefore a renegade in Druchii eyes. Any Dark Elves that Dijin is fighting against will suffer Hatred towards him.

specials.name: Wanderer
specials.description: Dijin Katal only ever stays with a warband for the duration of the battle. A warband who used Dijin Katal in their last battle may not seek him out until they have fought at least one battle without him.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any warband except for Amazons, Shadow Warriors, Dark Elves (obviously) and any warband that includes and type of Elven hired sword may hire Dijin Katal.

name: Doctor Doppler and Mr. Genag
description: The row's profile is Dr. Doppler's, his base form.

specials.name: A Test Subject
specials.description: Where a test subject is given instead of the gold upkeep, roll a dice: on any result other than a 6 he dies, and on a 6 he gains +1 Strength permanently. If he belonged to a henchmen group, make a group for him alone; if he was an enemy, he returns to his warband free of cost.

specials.name: Transformation
specials.description: At the beginning of each of his turns roll a dice: on a 5+ Dr. Doppler transforms into Mr. Genag. Once transformed, roll a dice at the beginning of each of his turns: on a 1-2 Mr. Genag transforms back. The transformation heals no wounds.

specials.name: Experimental Potions
specials.description:
Dr. Doppler is an academic and cannot wield weapons in close combat, but carries experimental potions. He may throw up to 3 per match, with a maximum range of 6". On a hit, roll a dice.

D6 | Result
1 | The potion does not shatter. If the target passes an Initiative test it adds the potion to its inventory and may use it until the end of the match.
2 | The potion has no effect.
3-5 | The potion explodes in flames: 2 automatic S3 hits on the target and 1 automatic S3 hit on every model within 2" of it.
6 | The potion deforms and mutates its victim. For the rest of the match the target's Strength, Toughness and Initiative are each reduced by 2, to a minimum of 1.

specials.name: Mr. Genag
specials.description: Mr. Genag's profile is M5 WS4 BS2 S5 T4 W3 I5 A2 Ld7. He uses no weapons or armour and suffers no penalty for it, and has the skills Sprint, Leap, Scale Sheer Surfaces and Combat Master.

specials.name: Great Physical Build
specials.description: Mr. Genag has a natural 5+ armour save against all attacks.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: The model causes fear.

specials.name: Evil
specials.description: Mr. Genag may attack knocked down or stunned enemies even while he is in combat with other models.

specials.name: Hates Spellcasters and Priests
specials.description: Mr. Genag hates all spellcasters and any model able to use Sigmar's prayers.

upkeep_fee.note: Or a test subject for the experiments, who may be a warband member or a captured enemy, so long as he is not undead, possessed or a mutant.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven and the Sisters of Sigmar may hire Dr. Doppler and Mr. Genag.

name: Drenok Johansen, Wielder of the Great Axe
description:
The great sagas of the Norse tribes tell of a mighty warrior known as the Wielder of the Great Axe. Long ago in the icy, inhospitable tundra of the Norse land a young clansman with fire in his eyes and passion in his heart left his clan in search of his father's fate. His father was Johan warrior-prime, Chieftain of the Clan Icefang, possessed by a demon of Khorne. His father had disappeared rumoured to have travelled across the seas. Leaving the clan in a self-imposed exile he was never seen again in the lands of his birth.

After many a long year within the realms of the Old World Drenok took ship to the New World in search of his father. Weeks dragged on into months and months into years until finally the day came when the two mortals finally crossed paths. Only then did Drenok truly know fear. For when Drenok looked into the face of his father he saw the Daemon within. A titanic struggle ensued between father and son. The battle was fierce and long, lasting for many hours. With each wound Drenok inflicted upon this demon, his father, anguish and rage consumed his soul. Finally his father fell and the battle was won. But this was no true victory, this was a day of mourning. For Drenok had now lost a part of his soul he could never reclaim. He gazed upon the great axe, which lay at the feet of his father's corpse and realised it to be the legendary axe of the Icefang, his clan. Lifting the mighty axe above his head, his hair braids blowing in the wind he roared in defiance of world. His quest would be to bring honour to the death of his father.

specials.name: Berserker
specials.description: If Drenok is reduced to zero wounds roll 1D6. On a score of 4+ he stands fighting until the end of the tum. You must roll every turn or he will be Out of Action.

specials.name: Icefang Axe
specials.description: A massive double-handed axe, this weapon has been handed down through the ancestors of Ice fang throughout the generations. It is said that a revered ancestor used the axe and slew a great White Dragon many centuries ago. The axe is the same as a double-handed weapon but it can also Parry and has a +1 modifier to injury rolls.

specials.name: Sabertooth Tiger Hide
specials.description: Gives Drenok a 6 save in close combat and 5+ against missile fire.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Norse and human warbands may hire Drenok.

specials.name: Sought Out
specials.description:
There is no hire fee. He comes to the aid of a warband that may hire him only if it sends one or more of its heroes to look for him in the normal manner, rolling under or equal to their Initiative. Found, he may still decide not to come, and comes only if the enemy warband has the higher rating. Roll a D6 and consult the table.

Difference in warband rating | D6 needed
0-49 | no chance
50-99 | 6+
100-149 | 5+
150-199 | 4+
200+ | 3+

specials.name: Facing Dwarfs or Strigoi
specials.description: Add 1 to the roll if the warband faces Dwarfs or Strigoi.

specials.name: Kutta and Smasha
specials.description: Eeza Ugezod wields an axe and a choppa; the extra attack for the additional hand weapon is already in his profile. Smasha is an Orc choppa, which gives him +1 Strength when he charges. As he carries two hand weapons he must choose which one he attacks with normally and which makes the additional attack.

specials.name: Raging Fury
specials.description: When Eeza Ugezod charges he attacks any enemy he can see. He charges and attacks as normal, but as soon as an enemy warrior suffers an injury he moves up to 2" to engage another enemy, so he may attack several enemy warriors in one charge. With no enemy model within 2" he moves 2" towards the closest one and any remaining attacks are wasted. This applies only when he charges, not in later rounds of combat and not when he is charged.

specials.name: Biggust
specials.description: Eeza Ugezod is automatically the leader of any warband he joins.

specials.name: Hates Dwarfs
specials.description: Eeza Ugezod hates all Dwarfs, and all Dwarfs hate him.

hire_fee.note: No hire fee: he must be sought out before the battle.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any Orc or Goblin warband may hire Eeza Ugezod.

specials.name: Hired with Her Sister
specials.description: Fleur and Estella may be hired at the same time without needing two Initiative rolls. They may not be fielded in the same game by separate warbands unless those warbands are allied or the scenario is Last Orders. If two opposing players both field them, both sisters leave the board and are removed from both warbands, taking the money with them.

specials.name: Main-Gauche
specials.description: Estella's main-gauche may be used as a dagger, for +1 attack, or to parry a single attack, with no attack. Used with another parrying weapon she may parry two attacks. The player chooses each turn.

specials.name: Princess of Parries
specials.description: If Estella has a higher Weapon Skill than her attacker she gets +1 on her parry rolls, so she can parry attacks that hit on a 6. She may also try to parry attacks made with double or more her Strength.

specials.name: Protective
specials.description: If Fleur is knocked down or stunned at the start of your turn, Estella will charge the enemy closest to Fleur, ignoring fear. While Fleur is knocked down or stunned, Estella fights, but does not move, as if she were frenzied. If Estella is not within charge range she moves 8" directly towards Fleur, with the normal deductions for terrain.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any non-chaotic, non-Skaven and non-Undead warband may hire Estella.

specials.name: Hired with Her Sister
specials.description: Fleur and Estella may be hired at the same time without needing two Initiative rolls. They may not be fielded in the same game by separate warbands unless those warbands are allied or the scenario is Last Orders. If two opposing players both field them, both sisters leave the board and are removed from both warbands, taking the money with them.

specials.name: Loaded Pistols
specials.description: Fleur's guns may be filled with refined powder or superior gun powder, as the player chooses.

specials.name: Pistolier Extraordinaire
specials.description: Fleur may either fire three shots in one turn and take one turn to reload, or fire and reload two shots each round.

specials.name: Bretonnian Blood
specials.description: When Fleur shoots a duelling pistol, the first 10" count as close range.

specials.name: Sheltered
specials.description: So long as Estella is on the board, Fleur is immune to fear.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any non-chaotic, non-Skaven and non-Undead warband may hire Fleur.

specials.name: Two Small Staffs
specials.description: Gaz Er Unga Og fights with two small staffs and may parry once with them. She wears no armour to begin with, but may be given some.

specials.name: Barbarian Shaman
specials.description: Gaz Er Unga Og knows all six spells of the Barbarian Shaman spell list.

specials.name: Magical Experimentalist
specials.description: Every time a spell is used while she is around, the enemy's included, she may try to adapt it. Roll a D6: on a 6 she has an idea of how the spell works, and if she uses it as her next spell and manages its difficulty she has learnt it. Even after she leaves the warband that first engaged her, she keeps every spell she has learnt and any item she was given during the campaign, so a second employer gets more for his money than the first.

specials.name: Knows the Land
specials.description: A warband that engages her always adds 2 to the roll to determine the supply source it reaches.

hire_fee.note: No gold: she claims an item from whoever hires her, a weapon or a magic item she has not met before, which must count as rare 8 or more.

upkeep_fee.note: Common items she does not know, anything civilised enough that barbarians cannot buy it. When the warband has no more to give her, or stops giving them, she leaves.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Every warband except Witch Hunters may hire Gaz Er Unga Og.

name: Grand Master Ippan Shu
description:
Although the populace of Sen’Quoi knows the name Ippan Shu, very few of them have ever seen him. Rumoured to be both a hundred years of age and a grand Master of the martial arts, he is also given supernatural aspects, such as the abilities of flight and the spitting of fire on those he calls foe.

His legend says that a former disciple, Xiao Lin, once tried to assassinate him as Ippan Shu lay sleeping. Still asleep, he fought his student, only awakening when a knife sliced of half his left moustache (a grave outrage, for a Cathayan elder’s beard represents his wisdom and experience). Angered, Shu immediately killed Xiao Lin, yet still he keeps his moustache trimmed short; The better to remind him that even the best can be found wanting and caught off-guard, that no matter how good you become, you can always be better.

A loner, Ippan Shu can be found wandering the Borderlands, meditating or fighting the different opponents that dwell therein, be they terrible creatures of Chaos or the ferocious hobgoblin wolf riders; he sees them all as a way of bettering his arts. Some whisper that Shu seeks to face an opponent who will prove a better fighter than he and, until that day, will continue his wanderings, whether he lives another hundred years or achieves the highest reaches of enlightenment.

Also has: Speed, Battle Monk.

specials.name: Bare-handed Fighting
specials.description: Ippan Shu can fight without weapons and suffers no penalties when doing so. In fact, he then counts as having a second close combat weapon and gets +1 attack.

specials.name: Iron Fan
specials.description: Ippan Shu’s iron fan can flick deadly force with the grace of a dance. The weapon grants him +1 Initiative and allows him to parry not only enemy blows but also missile shots (see below). Note that the Art of Silent Death skill applies to Lin’s fan attacks as well.

specials.name: Parry Missiles
specials.description: Ippan Shu may use his iron fan to parry missiles. For each hit by a missile weapon he parries the shot if he beats the 'to hit' roll. Note that Ippan Shu also has the Dodge skill.

specials.name: Immune to Psychology
specials.description: Ippan Shu is in total control of his emotions and therefore immune to psychology and automatically passes all Leadership-based tests.

specials.name: With the Elegance of a Feather
specials.description: Ippan Shu’s moves appear supernatural to his enemies, as if he was flying. When running or charging he may move up to half his total movement rate (ie, 6” – see Lightning Speed skill) in any direction, not only on the ground. This can be combined with the *leap* skill, thus allowing Ippan Shu to move up to 6+D6” in any direction. Note that he still must always finish his Movement on solid ground.

specials.name: Way of the Dragon
specials.description: Being one of the most perfectly trained mystic Dragon Monks, Ippan Shu spits fire upon his enemies in the shooting phase. Use the flame template to determine which models suffer an automatic Strength 4 hit. In addition, hit models are set on fire on a roll of 4+ (see “Fire Rules” section). Note that Ippan Shu can use his breath attack even when he is engaged in close combat.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any warband which includes Humans or Elves, including Battle Monks, may hire Ippan Shu, not including Dark Elves, Outlaws and Bandits.

specials.name: Sought Out
specials.description:
There is no hire fee. He comes to the aid of a warband that may hire him only if it sends one or more of its heroes to look for him in the normal manner, rolling under or equal to their Initiative. Found, he may still decide not to come, and comes only if the enemy warband has the higher rating. Roll a D6 and consult the table.

Difference in warband rating | D6 needed
0-49 | no chance
50-99 | 6+
100-149 | 5+
150-199 | 4+
200+ | 3+

specials.name: Facing Strigoi
specials.description: Add 1 to the roll if the warband faces Strigoi or a rebellious Skaven warband.

specials.name: Rivalry
specials.description: If a rival warband is hiring Alchec, add 2 to the roll to see whether Neekit will join. Even where the difference in ratings means no chance, he will come along on a 5+.

specials.name: Confident
specials.description: If Neekit wins two battles in succession he adds 1 to his Leadership, to a maximum of 10; if he loses two in succession he subtracts 1, to a minimum of 5.

specials.name: Magic of the Horned Rat
specials.description: Neekit is a wizard and knows every spell of the Magic of the Horned Rat as well as his own.

specials.name: Grey Seer
specials.description: Neekit is automatically the leader of any warband he joins.

specials.name: Master Sorcerer
specials.description: Neekit may keep casting spells until he fails to cast one. Each attempt after the first is at +1 difficulty, cumulatively. When he casts more than one spell in a turn, a failure means he has eaten too much warpstone and must roll on the Injury chart at once. He may not cast the same spell more than once in a turn.

specials.name: Staff of Authority
specials.description: While Neekit is not fleeing, stunned or out of action, any friendly Skaven warrior on the battlefield may use his Leadership.

specials.name: Wyrdstone Amulet
specials.description: Neekit's player may re-roll any one dice for Neekit once during a battle.

specials.name: Warpscroll
specials.description: Once per battle Neekit may read from the scroll. One model within 6" must take a Leadership test using his own Leadership or age rapidly and be put out of action at once. In the post-battle sequence that victim does not roll to see if he is seriously injured. A henchman is simply removed from the roster, though the warband may keep his equipment. For a hero, one characteristic chosen by the Skaven player is reduced by one, to a minimum of 1, and its maximum is reduced by one too. A warrior hit by a Warpscroll more than once has each characteristic affected only once.

specials.name: Neekit's Wares
specials.description:
If a warband has fought alongside Neekit at least once he may sell it Skalm and Skavenbrew, at a rarity of 7 each with the usual bonus for Streetwise. Both are one use only and he will let a warband own only one of each at a time.

Skalm, 20 gc: a thick black paste. At the end of each battle one Skaven warrior's wounds are automatically healed and he does not roll on the Serious Injury chart. Skalm works only on Skaven physiology, and Neekit himself has become immune to it. It is highly poisonous to non-Skaven and may be applied to weapons, with the same effects as Black Lotus; it cannot then also heal after that battle.

Skavenbrew, 30 gc: given to a Skaven warrior at the start of a battle if he wants it. Roll a D6: 1, no effect; 2-3, he hates all enemy warriors; 4-5, he is subject to frenzy; 6, he is subject to frenzy and hates all enemy warriors. A Skaven sorcerer who drinks it may cast no spells for that battle, even on a result of no effect. It has no effect on non-Skaven.

specials.name: Extra Spells
specials.description: Neekit may choose one of his own spells to add to the spells he may cast this battle. They affect friend and foe alike unless the spell says otherwise.

spells.name: Death Frenzy
spells.description: Difficulty 8. A Skaven warrior is automatically affected and gains +2 Movement, +2 Attacks and +2 Initiative. At the beginning of each of his turns he must take a Toughness test or suffer a wound. At the end of the battle he runs off in temporary madness and must roll on the Serious Injury table; a henchman must also take a Toughness test or die. The spell may be cast on an enemy Skaven warrior.

spells.name: Pestilent Breath
spells.description: Difficulty 5. One model within 3" must take a Toughness test or go out of action. If Neekit rolls a double when casting it he suffers a wound with no save, and recovers automatically after the battle if he goes out of action from it.

spells.name: Poison Wind
spells.description: Difficulty 11. A poisonous wind blows in a straight line away from Neekit. Any model in its path must take a Toughness test or roll on the Injury chart, treating out of action as stunned.

spells.name: Skitterleap
spells.description: Difficulty 7. Neekit teleports in any direction. Place a marker in that direction and roll 3D6 for the distance in inches. If he would land in a solid object he has teleported to his inner sanctum and counts as out of action with no injury roll, and must be hired again if the warband wants him back.

spells.name: Veil of Darkness
spells.description: Difficulty 7. One enemy warrior within 12" is blinded: his Weapon Skill is reduced to 1 and he may not attack, shoot or cast spells, and may only walk, at half pace. At the end of each of his turns he may take a Leadership test to shake the spell off.

spells.name: Wither
spells.description: Difficulty 8. Neekit may give up all his normal attacks to make a single attack at twice his normal Strength. Roll to hit as normal. The victim may make no dodge, armour or ward save of any kind.

hire_fee.note: No hire fee: he must be sought out before the battle.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any Skaven warband may hire Grey Seer Neekit.

name: Heinrich 'Altdorf' Schmidt
description:
Dr. Heinrich Schmidt is renowned at the University of Altdorf. However, most of this renown is not out of his scholarly works, but rather the priceless artifacts he sends home from his journeys. Thanks to him, artifacts from Kislev or Norsca, as well as far off places­ such as Cathay and Lustria have found their way home to Altdorf. Since all his findings are shipped back to Altdorf, this has earned him the nickname 'Altdorf' Schmidt. His main arena for relic hunting however, has come to be in Araby and Khemri, with its grand tombs and priceless treasures. The acquisition of the relics is not often discussed, as most of the scholars agree that they are more capable of appreciating them than the inhabitants of the lands from which they came.

Also has: Tomb Explorer, Whip Master, Mule Skinner listing.

specials.name: Oh no, not Snakes!
specials.description: 'Altdorf' fears all snakes and serpents.

specials.name: Whip Swing
specials.description: 'Altdorf' Schmidt has developed a technique to use his whip as a rope to swing over gaps. To represent this, 'Altdorf' Schmidt can jump a gap (up to a maximum of 4'), without deducting the distance jumped from his normal Movement allowance. You must, however, still make an Initiative test not fall down. In addition, he may use his whip to jump to a lower level, even through windows. However, there must always be something on a higher level to attach the whip to in order of swing with it (just use common sense here - sewers, dungeons, tunnels, etc, always count as having something to attach the whip to). If 'Altdorf' Schmidt falls into a pit trap, he may try to use his whip to save himself from falling down by passing an Initiative test.

specials.name: No time for you
specials.description: 'Altorf' Schmidt is notorious for bejng a man in a hurry. If his charge path toward a hero, treasure or some other important target is obstructed by an enemy henchman who would prevent his charge, 'Altdorf' Schmidt may attempt a single shot with his Duelling Pistol before charging (assuming he didn't fire it last round of course). If this shot knocks down, stuns or takes the henchman out of action, 'Altdorf' Schmidt may charge as if the henchman wasn't there. If the enchman is unharmed, it counts as a failed charge as normal.

specials.name: I'll Take That!
specials.description: Rather than being paid in gold, 'Altorf' collects relics and artifacts from the places he visits. His upkeep cost is taken as a piece of treasure.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any Human warband may hire Altdorf Schmidt.

specials.name: Sought Out
specials.description:
There is no hire fee. He comes to the aid of a warband that may hire him only if it sends one or more of its heroes to look for him in the normal manner, rolling under or equal to their Initiative. Found, he may still decide not to come, and comes only if the enemy warband has the higher rating. Roll a D6 and consult the table.

Difference in warband rating | D6 needed
0-49 | no chance
50-99 | 6+
100-149 | 5+
150-199 | 4+
200+ | 3+

specials.name: Archer Extraordinaire
specials.description: Im Abav Yub may combine the Nimble and Quick Shot skills, so he may move and shoot twice with his bow.

specials.name: Never Armoured
specials.description: The model never wears armour.

specials.name: Gu Ag, Unga Zag and Leggit Er
specials.description: His bow Gu Ag and his sword Unga Zag are a bow and a sword. His cape Leggit Er counts as an Elven cloak.

hire_fee.note: No hire fee: he must be sought out before the battle.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Im Abav Yub will only join Albion Barbarian tribes.

name: Innominatus, the Tilean Gladiator
description:
"You ask for my name? Many has asked and none who have done so have lived. Come and ask with your blade, and let us find out!"

Innominatus, the Cursed Gladiator. The Unnamed. The Scourge of the Red Sands. This hulking Tilean pit fighter is known by many names, and his origin is shrouded in mystery and whispered legends. His face is hidden by an ancient helmet which he never removes, though those who claim that they have fought him and survived tell tales of hideous scars and unblinking eyes beneath the steel faceplate. He is festooned with countless weapons and pieces of armour -trophies of his countless victories, further adding to his fearsome reputation.

Minstrels tell many conflicting stories of his origin: some say he once drank from the Well of Eternal Youth, but was cursed by gods for his hubris, doomed to an eternal life of bloodshed. Others say he once killed an evil necromancer in a duel who cursed him to walk the earth until he meets a warrior who can match his prowess in arms. None dare to ask Innominatus whether these tales have any truth to them.

The war-cries of innominatus still echo the creed of the ancient arenas of Tilea, using an accent not heard in a millennia. In the oldest of ruins of the ancient Tilean coliseums engravings show pictures of a gladiator Innominatus who once rose to fame when emperors still ruled Luccini. If he is indeed the same gladiator who once ruled the bloodied sands of Remas, he is must surely be a product of some ancient curse.

In these days of strife, the violence and the thrill of the kill has attracted Innominatus to Mordheim, where can be found in the squalid Fighting Pits, eternally looking for someone who could match him in single combat. To this end, he relentlessly seeks a duel with Aenur, the Sword of Twilight, but the Elf bladesman shows no interest in bloodsports. Thus Innominatus is willing to hire his services to warbands striking into the depths of Mordheim itself, hoping to find the Elf warrior and finally founding out once and for all who of them is the true Lord of War.

Many a famed warrior has met their end by suddenly running into Innominatus amongst the ruins of the Cursed City, compelled into a duel only to become yet another bloody epitaph in the legend of Innominatus.

specials.name: Pit Master
specials.description: To survive in the pit you need to think fast and act even faster! Innominatus to survive so many fights as gained an incredible ability and speed to avoid enemy strikes and shots: He can avoid any hit from close combat and missile weapons on a D6 roll of 4+. Note that this roll is taken as soon as a hit is scored (shooting and close combat) to see whether the Innominatus dodges it or not, before rolling to wound, and before any effects from other skills or equipment (such as lucky charms).

specials.name: Who is the hero?
specials.description: Once per battle Innominatus can challenge any opponent hero, hired sword or Dramatis Personae on the battlefield to engage in a mortal duel (yes, including the leader and even if not in sight or hidden! Innominatus starts roaming across the streets shouting out the hero’s name with all sorts of wares!). If the opponent player refuses the duel the challenged hero, hired sword or Dramatis Personae is removed immediately from the battlefield. The challenged character is so scared to fight against Innominatus he prefers to run away and to hide so far away he will also miss the next game. If he accepts the challenge resolve the fight immediately. Roll to see which side charges and fight the battle as normal. Innominatus will benefit from the Pit Fighter skill. If Innominatus wins, see Thumbs Up/Thumbs Down rule, and his upkeep is halved to 20gc for this game. If the opponent wins remove Innominatus immediately from the battlefield, roll for injuries as usual and place the winning hero in his previous position. The hero or hired sword gains also 3XP for winning against a such great opponent.

specials.name: Thumbs Up/Thumbs Down
specials.description:
If Innominatus wins the fight, the looser is not immediately removed as out of action, the loosing player has the chance to decide if his hero will live or die!

- Thumbs Up: The life of the looser is saved but Innominatus will take as a trophy all the hero’s equipment, leaving him naked and shaking in the middle of the arena. Place the looser in his previous position but he is so shocked he will be subject to stupidity for the rest of the game (unless it is immune to psychology).
- Thumbs Down: Mercy is rare in the arena, Innominatus takes his blood tribute and the looser is slain. Remove the looser immediately from the battlefield and from the warband roster. All the heroes of the looser’s warband gain 1XP (having seen Innominatus in action has been a great lesson!) and the loosing player retains all the equipment of the dead model.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven and Dark Elves may hire Innominatus.

specials.name: Thrice Spittin'
specials.description: Iñigo may shoot two pistols in one turn, as the Pistolier skill allows, and then shoot with his third the next turn while reloading the first two.

specials.name: Dastardly Bravado
specials.description: Each successful hit with his pistols gives Iñigo +1 Ballistic Skill, to a maximum of 6. If he misses a shot or gets stuck, his Ballistic Skill returns to its original value. He may raise it again with later hits.

specials.name: Ah Mathann, Not Again!
specials.description: At the beginning of each turn roll a single dice. On a 2-6 nothing happens. On a 1 Iñigo's peg leg gets stuck and he may not move at all until he frees it. While stuck he may shoot or fight as normal. To free himself he must spend a turn doing so and may not fight or shoot during it, and while he is freeing himself an enemy wanting to target him must first pass a Leadership test and otherwise target someone else if it can. Undead and animals do not take this test.

specials.name: Blessing Nonetheless
specials.description: Each time a wound is allocated to Iñigo, roll a dice: on a 6 the wound is negated. This 6+ save may not be modified and is taken after normal armour saves. If the peg leg stops a wound while he is stuck, he is freed at once; he is also freed if he is knocked down or stunned.

specials.name: Golden Greed
specials.description: When a warband holding Iñigo loses, the winning player may try to bribe him away. If the losing player wants to keep him he must say so; otherwise the winner simply pays Iñigo's upkeep and he joins him. If both want him, each writes down an amount of gold, at least 25, without showing the other; they are revealed together and Iñigo joins whoever offered more, and the other pays nothing. If both offer exactly the same, Iñigo takes both bribes and leaves, and may be found again after D3 games.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven, Undead, the Possessed and Ogres may hire Iñigo. He will also refuse to work alongside any ogre.

specials.name: Not Two Games Running
specials.description: Jeremiah Bane will not work for the same warband two games in a row.

specials.name: Immune to Psychology
specials.description: The model is immune to psychology and never leaves combat.

specials.name: Immune to Poison
specials.description: Not affected by any poison.

specials.name: Ethereal (Jeremiah Bane)
specials.description: Jeremiah Bane has a 4+ unmodifiable save against all attacks. It may not be used with Dodge or Step Aside, and has no effect against magical attacks, artefacts, gromril, ithilmar and silver bullets among them. He may also take a Leadership test to move through any object, or even to walk on water; if he fails that test while standing on water he counts as taken out of action, sinking to the seafloor.

specials.name: Festooned with Pistols (Jeremiah Bane)
specials.description: Jeremiah Bane carries so many double-barrelled pistols that he never has to reload, and always has a new one primed and ready to fire. In hand-to-hand combat he may only use pistols in the first round; in later rounds he draws his swords. He may draw another pair of pistols once he is out of combat, or once all of his opponents are knocked down or stunned.

specials.name: Dread Pirate
specials.description: Any model wishing to board a boat Jeremiah Bane is on must first pass a fear test. This does not stack with Terrifying.

specials.name: Terrifying
specials.description: Jeremiah Bane causes fear in all models, even those that already cause fear or are immune to psychology. Only daemons and undead models are immune.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Undead warbands may hire Jeremiah Bane: Undead, Tomb Guardians, Ghost Pirates, Necrarchs, a Liche warband and the like.

name: Johann the Knife
description:
Of the many cutthroats and assassins for hire that infest the settlements around Mordheim, Johann the Knife is the most famous. He exhibits his vocation as hired knife-fighter and assassin extraordinaire by the various lethal-looking daggers hanging from his belt, and the mean glint of his eyes. Johann wears dark leather gear, slightly out of fashion, which has never been washed (or so the barmaids say). His long face bears the scars of many a fight, and his unkempt hair is lank and greasy.

Johann’s purse is always heavy with gold, and he takes no trouble to hide it, since only a fool would try to steal it from him. Many have tried, and all have died… very quickly. The craftsmanship and quality of Johann’s daggers is beyond compare, as he has taken them from the bodies of the many wealthy, but unskillful, opponents he has despatched in vicious duels.

Also carries: Throwing Knives.
Also has: Knife Fighter.

specials.name: Hiring Fee
specials.description: Johann is addicted to Crimson Shade, so you may hire him for one portion of Crimson Shade if you wish.

specials.name: Knife Fighter Extraordinaire
specials.description: Johann has a deserved reputation for being the greatest knifefighter in whole of the Empire. Unlike normal warriors, he can combine the Knife Fighter and Quick Shot skills (yes, he can throw six throwing knives in one turn if he does not move!).

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven, Undead and the Possessed may hire Johann.

name: Khar-mel the Djinn
description:
Djinn are magical elemental spirits akin to Daemons, that reside in the deep deserts of Araby and the Land of the Dead. They may be summoned by a complicated ritual involving dark pacts and unholy promises. Djinn are creatures born of the elements and may assume many different forms such as horses made of sand, pillars of fire or mighty Arabic warriors comprised of swirling air. As with all Daemons, anyone learning a Djinn's true name will receive great power over it. Djinn are ancient spirits and know many long forgotten secrets, especially from the early days of Nehekhara and for this reason many sorcerers and priests attempt to summon them to learn such forbidden knowledge. Sultan Jaffar was known to have been in prolonged contact with some of the mightiest Djinn, although many surmise that their lies led to his downfall.

Khar-mel is one of the few known Djinn of Araby. She has oft been encountered in the western desert over the centuries. Despite being centuries old, she normally appears as a beautiful arabian woman of about 30 years of age, although she has been known to appear as a swirling cloud of dust or a pillar of fire on occasion.

Like all Djinn, Khar-mel knows many secrets forgotten by mortal man and many sorcerers and priests have tried to summon her to answer their questions. If she does have one weakness it is her thirst for knowledge. A warband who claims that they are undertaking a quest in search of ancient lore may well secure Khar-mel's services.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: The Djinn naturally radiate an aura of power and cause fear.

specials.name: Ethereal
specials.description: Khar-mel has only a semi-solid form and has a 5+ save that is never be modified due to high Strength or anything else. The save is not effective against magical weapons.

specials.name: Elemental Magic
specials.description: Khar-mel knows D3 spells chosen from the Elemental Magic list. Roll randomly on the Elemental magic list to determine the spells she may use.

specials.name: Whirlwind
specials.description: Khar-mel has the power to turn into a whirlwind. This can take many forms: a sandstorm, a pillar of fire or a hazy shimmer in the air. She can run at triple her movement but may not charge or be charged. She cannot make any attacks or cast spells while using this power, but is at -1 to hit with missile weapons.

specials.name: Djinn's Curse
specials.description: Djinn are incredibly ancient creatures, prophets of fate and doom to many. This interferes with all of the Djinn's enemies within 4", incurring a -1 penalty to their to-hit rolls (both with missiles and with close combat weapons) and all saves.

specials.name: Djinn's Luck
specials.description: Djinn have been around for centuries and due to their prophetic powers are very good at avoiding trouble. This power confers a 4+ Ward save. If no save normally applies (eg, against magic weapons) then she gains a 6+ save.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any warband may hire Khar-mel. However in order to summon her, a Wizard (or other spell caster, including a Priest) must pass a test on his own Leadership. This Wizard may be a Hired Sword, but must have been with the warband for at least one battle prior to attempting to summon Khar-mel. If the Wizard that summoned Khar-mel is killed or leaves the warband, Khar-mel will leave as well.

specials.name: War Frenzy
specials.description: Kromwell is frenzied. If he is knocked down or stunned he becomes frenzied again during your next recovery phase.

specials.name: Loner
specials.description: Kromwell is immune to All Alone.

specials.name: Hard Head and Hard to Kill
specials.description: Kromwell ignores the Concussion rule, and is only taken out of action on a 6: a 5 counts as a stunned result, as for other Dwarfs.

specials.name: Possessed
specials.description: After each game in which Kromwell took at least one enemy warrior out of action, roll a Leadership test, deducting one point from his Leadership for each enemy he took out in close combat. If the test is failed he charges and fights a random hero from your roster for 3 rounds, then leaves, and may not be used next game. If that warrior takes him out within those 3 rounds, Kromwell will stay with the warband if you wish to pay upkeep for him.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any evil warband may hire Kromwell.

specials.name: Anchor
specials.description: Krushj's anchor counts as an axe and as a rope and hook.

specials.name: Fear
specials.description: The model causes fear.

specials.name: Large
specials.description: This unit is treated as a Large Target. They may always be shot at with ranged weapons with a +1 modifier to hit.

specials.name: Brace of Handguns
specials.description: Krushj is so large that he counts his handguns as mere pistols, so Pistolier applies to them. They have a 24" range, Strength 4 and an extra -1 save, and fire every other turn. They are move or fire weapons because of his size.

specials.name: Giant Parrot
specials.description: In the first round of combat the parrot gives all of Krushj's opponents -1 to hit in close combat, unless they pass a Leadership test. It may also make a single attack with Weapon Skill 3 and Strength 2.

upkeep_fee.note: Half of it is spent on birdseed.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Krushj does not work for Skaven or Undead warbands; otherwise he will work for anyone with enough money.

name: Laure Croftenssen
description: Also carries: the Adventurer's Pair of Handguns and a rifle.

specials.name: Handgun Expert
specials.description: Laure may shoot twice in a round with any pair of handguns.

specials.name: No Armour
specials.description: Laure wears no armour.

specials.name: Hates the Undead
specials.description: Laure hates the undead.

specials.name: Loner
specials.description: Laure suffers no ill effect from fighting alone against several enemies.

specials.name: Adventurer's Pair of Handguns
specials.description: 50 gc, rarity 11. Range 8", Strength 4, -2 armour save, fast reload. Fast reload: Laure may fire once in every shooting phase, as with a normal pair of handguns, and in close combat she may either make two attacks in the first round and then pick up another weapon, or make one attack in every round of combat.

hire_fee.note: 40 gc to a Sisters of Sigmar warband.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any non-evil warband may hire Laure Croftenssen.

name: Le Roi Ballaume
description: Ballaume le Brave, Bretonnian King-in-exile, and Geoffroy, Duke of the Nameless Dukedom, hired as a pair. The row's profile is Ballaume's.

specials.name: The Beastslayer of Fronsac
specials.description: Ballaume is not the one the sword deems worthy, so it counts as a magical sword that gives +1 to any parry roll, which means he can block an enemy to-hit roll of 6. Were he not a cursed outcast banished by the Fey Enchantress, it would instead give +2 Weapon Skill, +4 Strength, an automatic Master Strike on any critical hit, and strike first.

specials.name: The Chalice of Fate
specials.description: Whenever Ballaume is not bound in close combat he may drink from the chalice once per turn, which gives him one D6 re-roll to use at any point. For every re-roll he uses, the opposing player may force Ballaume's player to re-roll any other D6 roll in the game, re-rolls excepted; that result cannot be modified in any way and must be accepted.

specials.name: Geoffroy, Duke of the Nameless Dukedom
specials.description: Geoffroy's profile is M4 WS4 BS3 S4 T3 W2 I4 A2 Ld8. He carries heavy armour, a helmet, a shield and the Banner of the Exile, and has the skills Unstoppable Charge, Resilient and Combat Master.

specials.name: The Banner of the Exile
specials.description: The banner combines the rules of a banner, so friendly warriors within 12" may re-roll any failed All Alone test, and of a spear, so it strikes first and its bearer may only carry a shield or buckler in the other hand. It also counts as magical.

specials.name: Armour Proficient
specials.description: Ballaume and Geoffroy suffer no movement penalty for their armour.

specials.name: Unbreakable Ties
specials.description: The two must be hired as a pair and stay within 4" of each other. Should either be taken out of action, the other stands guard over his fallen comrade: he may stay still or move at half speed, dragging him along, and either way he may not attack, though he defends himself as normal.

specials.name: Doomed to Entropy
specials.description: Ballaume and Geoffroy are immune to any effect from the injury table, any curse, any special rule and any other effect lasting more than one game, and their equipment can never be permanently lost or stolen; anything taken during a game is returned after it. They can therefore never gain experience or new skills, and may never be given new equipment of any kind. They may also take no part in a scenario set outside the walls of Mordheim.

specials.name: Oath of Penitence
specials.description: In any Bretonnian warband, Ballaume and Geoffroy may never benefit from the Blessing of the Lady.

specials.name: You Owe Me, You Serve Me
specials.description: Should a warband ever fail to pay Ballaume his upkeep, the warband leader must at once roll on the Injury chart, rolling again for Dead, Robbed, Bitter Enmity, Captured and Sold to the Pits. Until the whole of the upkeep owed is paid, Ballaume counts as the leader of the warband, which may take it over its maximum of heroes, and the former leader is treated as a normal hero.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any non-Chaos human warband except the Sisters of Sigmar and Witch Hunters, and any Elf or Dwarf warband, may hire the two.

name: Leonardo da Miragliano
description: Also carries a steam pistol, a flash bomb and a magnifying monocle, whose rules are below.

specials.name: Sigismund's Scintillating Steam Pistol
specials.description: Range special, Strength 3, shot 12", armour piercing, prepare shot. Shot: use the blunderbuss rules at the range given.

specials.name: Leonardo's Incapacitating Flash Bomb
specials.description: Range 10", Strength 5, thrown weapon, armour piercing, nonlethal. Nonlethal: if it inflicts the last wound on a model, any out of action result counts as stunned instead.

specials.name: Magliano's Magnificent Magnifying Monocle
specials.description: Leonardo can spot hidden enemies within twice his Initiative in inches.

specials.name: Master Engineer
specials.description: Leonardo's modifications add 3" to the range of the warband's pistols and 6" to that of its other gunpowder weapons; the steam pistol is not affected. This cannot be combined with any other range increase, and the increases last only while he stays with the warband.

hire_fee.note: He may instead be hired with one item of rarity 10 or higher.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Any warband except Skaven, Undead and the Possessed may hire Leonardo.

name: Luthor the Looter
description: Luthor has ever found one true love in his entire life: his love for gold and luxuries that would put even a Dwarf King to shame. He has an amazing knack of finding the Warbands who are exploring the areas of Mordheim where plenty of loot still abounds. He readily offers his services to such, always looking for a way to grab the riches for himself. In battle, he uses every dirty trick and underhanded ploy to wriggle free from any combat in order to focus on what really matters -looting every last inch of the City of the Damned!

specials.name: I Ain't Got Time For You!
specials.description: Luthor is on a mission and has no time for frivolities such as melee combat. Luthor always succeeds when checking if he can escape from combat.

specials.name: Looter
specials.description:
Whenever Luthor enters a new building (as long as he is not Down or engaged in combat), he finds D6 Gold Crowns worth of loot -this can be done only once per building.

Add this to a running tally. If at the end of the battle, the leader of the Warband has to take a Leadership check. If successful, the warband gains half of the gold Luthor found. If the check fails, Luthor keeps all the looted gold!

specials.name: Mordheim Guide
specials.description:
Luthor knows Mordheim better than almost any man alive. When rolling on Exploration chart, you may consult Luthor. If you do so, you may add +1 Dice to the total of Exploration dice rolled, and once you have rolled all the dice, you can change one dice to match any other result rolled.

If you use this ability ( +1 Dice and the adjustment), the leader of your warband has to take a Leadership check. If you fail, then ignore the result on the Exploration Chart as Luthor finds the location alone and takes everything for himself! You still gain standard income and Wyrdstone as normal.

dramatis_persona.unique_to: Luthor can be hired by any warband with no exceptions.

name: Luthor Wolfenbaum
description:
Luthor Wolfenbaum is known by many illustrious names, all invented by himself to enhance his reputation. He offers his services to anyone and everyone, and dons one of his many and varied garbs to best match the needs of a warband looking for help, and often uses an eyepatch on either of his eyes to enhance his disguises. He alternately claims to be the greatest swordsman in all of the Empire, an invincible bowman, or a great dark wizard when a less savoury warband is looking to bolster their ranks. In reality Luthor is none of these things, but he usually finds a way to hoodwink the Warband long enough with a combination of backstabbing, cunning, ruthlessness and sleight of hand to claim his pouch of gold before disappearing into the shadows, looking for a new Warband to gullible enough to pay for his services.

Luthor, the Crimson Blade of Reikland: Most commonly, Luthor approaches new Warbands and claims to be the Crimson Blade of Reikland, the most fearsome swordsman between the sea and the World’s Edge Mountains, extorting a hefty price of gold for his services.

Luthor, the Dark Wizard Extraordinaire: When Luthor hears that a Warband is looking for a master of the mystic arts, he grabs his “magical” staff decorated with a nailed fish, and starts ranting in a mixture of Tilean, Estalian, Norse and Bretonnian with Reikspiel swear words thrown in, claiming that these are “magic spells”. In this alter ego Luthor can offer his services even to the more unsavoury warbands such as the Undead who are looking for magical help in the dark corners of the settlements like Cutthroat’s Haven or the Dragon’s Demise. In battle the Dark Wizard Luthor fights with clay orbs filled with Tilean Fire. Luthor throws these missiles with great accuracy and claims that they are fireballs conjured with his mystic powers.
